summary: Vipul Jadav is an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. in Sanskrit at Shree Somnath Sanskrit University (2017-2021). In 2020, he served as an Assistant Professor at the same institution.
Virchand Gandhi (1864-1901) was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai (~1880-1884), and later taught Herbert Warren.
Virendra Kumar Varma worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under traditional teachers Ramnath Dixit and Gopal Chandra Mishra, and he taught Kamala Prasad Tripathi.
Virendra Kumar Verma worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under teachers Ramanatha Dikshita and Gopal Chandra Mishra, and he taught Kamala Prasad Mishra.

Virendra Nath Misra (1935-2015) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Lucknow (~1953-1957) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1958-1961), later serving as Director of Deccan College (~1990-2000).

Indologist Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar (1887-1943) studied at St. Xavier's, St John's, Edinburgh, and Berlin (under Heinrich Lüders). He served with the Archaeological Survey of India (1915-1919) and became General Editor of the Mahabharata critical edition at BORI in 1925.

Vishva Bandhu (1897-1973), an Indologist and linguist, studied under Alfred Cooper Woolner (~1918-1920). He was Founder-Principal of Dayanand Brahma Mahavidyalaya (1921), Director of Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College (1934), and Director of the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute (~1924-1973).

Vishvanath Narayan Mandlik (1833-1899) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Elphinstone College (~1847-1851). He served as Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and was an examiner at the University of Mumbai.

Vishwa Nath Pathak (1926-2003) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He served as a professor at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1973-1978 and 1987).

Vishwanath Prasad Varma (born 1924) is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under Dhirendra Mohan Datta (~1942-1944), Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, doctoral supervisor Kali Kinkar Datta (~1948-1950), and Joachim Wach (1950).

Indologist Vishwanathan Venkatachalam (1925-2002) studied at Madras, Nagpur, and Vikram universities. He directed the Scindia Oriental Institute (~1972-1985) and served as vice-chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1986-1989, 1992-1995) and Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1996-1998).

Vitalij Petrovič Furnika (1940-1993) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Semën Gesselevič Rudin (1965), attended Saint Petersburg State University (1965-1970), and studied at the University of Madras (1969-1970).

Vittore Pisani (1899-1990) was an Italian linguist and Indologist who studied at Sapienza University of Rome under Carlo Formichi and Antonino Pagliaro. He held academic posts at Florence, Cagliari, Bocconi, and notably the University of Milan (1938-1969).
Vittorio Bettei worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a teacher of Latin and Greek at Liceo Ginnasio Benedetto Cairoli and Liceo Canova.

Vittorio Rocca (1862-1905) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Pisa (~1880-1885). He held a libera docenza in Sanskrit at Pisa in 1905 and served as a Docent at Sapienza University of Rome.

Indologist Vitus Angermeier studied at the University of Vienna under Karin Preisendanz, Chlodwig H. Werba, and Roque Mesquita. He served as a Lecturer at the University of Vienna (2022-2025) and a researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2025-2026).

Vlad Bănățeanu (1900-1963) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Chernivtsi, Bucharest, EPHE, and INALCO under scholars including Antoine Meillet and Émile Benveniste. He held posts at Chernivtsi University (1932) and the University of Bucharest (~1948-1963).

Vladimir Aleksandrovich Chernyshev (1927-1999) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Moscow State University (~1948-1953). He taught at MGIMO (1952-1956) and became a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies in 1956.

Vladimir Balabushevich (1900-1970) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested 1970, 1990).

Vladimir Druzhinin works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Novosibirsk State Medical University (2003-2009) and RUDN (2013-2016), serving as an assistant at Novosibirsk State Medical University (2009) and Novosibirsk State University (2015).
